quienes.titulo: A path to look at yourself calmly
quienes.texto: We believe no one should face the big questions alone: whether their life has meaning, whether they're using their time well, whether they're free to choose and whether they're truly accompanied. We exist to walk with you as you turn what weighs on you today into clarity, from your everyday life.

manifiesto.texto: We believe we all carry something we haven't told anyone. We believe looking at it is not sinking: it's the first step to transforming it. We believe you don't need to be at your limit to ask for help, or to have it all clear to begin. We believe the extraordinary begins on any ordinary Tuesday, with a small decision. We don't have magic answers and we won't tell you who you should be. We will listen without judging, tell you things straight and walk with you step by step. You decide, you act and you transform. We walk with you, today, from wherever you are.

pilares.texto: Put a name to what you live, without judgment.

perfil.sobre: I'm Pablo Gómez, a Colombian psychologist with a master's degree in family educational counseling. For more than ten years I have accompanied individuals and families: first in teaching and personal formation, and since 2019 in clinical work, where I worked in addiction rehabilitation and mental health, with workshops for parents and guidance on school dynamics. I now live in Australia, so I know what it is to start from scratch far from home. My way of working is close and direct: I listen without judging, I tell you things straight and I give you clear tools. You decide, you act and you transform. I walk beside you.

temas.pista: Tap a topic to see a short description and take a traffic-light check-in.
temas.checkTitulo: How are you doing with this topic?
temas.checkIntro: Tick the statements that sound like you over the last two weeks. There are no right or wrong answers.
temas.aviso: This check-in is only a guide to help you know yourself better. It is not a diagnosis and does not replace seeing a professional. No data is saved or sent.
temas.crisisTexto: If you feel you might harm yourself or you are in danger, don't wait:

verde.titulo: With {tema}, for now you are taking care of yourself

amarillo.titulo: With {tema}, it is worth paying attention

rojo.titulo: With {tema}, it is a good moment to ask for support

textos.verde: If you want to keep looking after yourself, you can talk with a professional about {tema}. The first listening session is free.
textos.amarillo: Working on {tema} early makes a difference. The first listening session is free.
textos.rojo: We can start working on {tema} as soon as possible. The first listening session is free.

ansiedad.descripcion: Excessive worry that is hard to control, present on most days for at least six months, together with restlessness, tiredness, muscle tension or trouble concentrating and sleeping that affect your daily life.
preguntas: I worry a lot, almost every day, and find it hard to stop those thoughts.
My body feels tense: racing heart, a knot in my stomach or shortness of breath.
I have trouble sleeping because my mind won't stop.
I avoid places, people or tasks because they make me nervous.
I feel irritable or restless without knowing exactly why.
Anxiety is affecting my work, my studies or my relationships.

resultados.verde: For now, anxiety doesn't seem to dominate your day-to-day. Even so, looking after your rest, moving and taking mindful breaks helps keep it from growing.
resultados.amarillo: There are signs of anxiety that are starting to weigh on you: worry, tension or restless sleep. It is a good moment to learn to regulate it before it limits you further.
resultados.rojo: Your body and mind have been on alert for a while, and anxiety is already affecting your life. With support you can learn concrete tools to lower that alert.

depresion.descripcion: Depressed mood or loss of interest nearly all day, for at least two weeks, with changes in sleep or appetite, tiredness, guilt or trouble concentrating, significantly affecting your daily life.
preguntas: I feel sad, empty or hopeless most of the day.
I lost interest or enjoyment in things I used to like.
I feel constantly tired and find it hard to start anything.
My sleep or appetite has changed noticeably.
I feel guilty or worthless, or I criticize myself harshly.
I have thought it would be better not to be alive, or about hurting myself.

resultados.verde: For now your mood seems to be holding you up. Keep your routines, your contact with others and what you enjoy; if you notice lasting changes, check in again.
resultados.amarillo: There are signs of low mood worth looking at closely: tiredness, loss of interest or changes in sleep. Talking about it early often keeps it from deepening.
resultados.rojo: What you describe suggests low mood is already weighing heavily on your life. Asking for professional help is a way of taking care of yourself, and depression can be treated.

estres.descripcion: Not a DSM-5 diagnosis: it describes extreme exhaustion, distance from work and lower performance after prolonged stress. If the distress follows a specific stressor, it may fit an adjustment disorder.
preguntas: I end the day exhausted, even after sleeping or resting on the weekend.
I find it hard to switch off from work, even outside working hours.
I feel that nothing I do at work has meaning or value anymore.
I have become more irritable, cynical or distant with colleagues or clients.
I have headaches, back pain or stomach problems that seem linked to stress.
I often think about leaving everything, but I don't know how to stop.

resultados.verde: Right now your work seems to be in a manageable balance. Look after your breaks, your schedule and your rest to keep it that way.
resultados.amarillo: Work is already taking its toll: tiredness, disconnection or irritability. Setting limits and recovering energy now helps you avoid burnout.
resultados.rojo: You are reaching a point of work burnout that rest alone won't fix. Professional support can help you recover and decide what to change.

pareja.descripcion: The DSM-5 recognizes relationship problems with a partner: conflict, distance and poor communication. A breakup can lead to an adjustment disorder, distress out of proportion that appears within three months of the change.
preguntas: We argue often and the fights repeat without reaching a solution.
I feel I can't be myself or say what I think with my partner.
There is silence, distance or a lack of trust between us.
After a breakup, I find it hard to stop thinking about that person.
I'm afraid of being alone or of losing that relationship.
This is costing me sleep, concentration or the desire to do things.

resultados.verde: Your relationship, or your process after a breakup, shows no major warning signs. Talking honestly and caring for your own space helps keep it that way.
resultados.amarillo: There is tension in your relationship, or in your grief after a breakup, that deserves attention. Working on it early keeps it from becoming patterns that are hard to change.
resultados.rojo: The conflict or pain in your relationship is already affecting your well-being. A professional space, alone or as a couple, helps you sort out what you feel and decide with clarity.

dependencia.descripcion: Not a DSM-5 diagnosis. It is described as an excessive need to be taken care of, leading to giving up decisions, fearing abandonment and tolerating mistreatment; it resembles dependent personality disorder.
preguntas: I find it hard to make decisions without asking that person or without their approval.
I put aside my plans, my friends or my interests so as not to lose them.
I put up with things that hurt me for fear of being abandoned.
When I don't hear from that person, I feel very anxious or empty.
I feel my worth depends on being loved or needed.
I take care of other people's problems so much that I forget my own.

resultados.verde: For now your relationships seem to leave you room to be yourself. Keep looking after your own decisions, friendships and interests.
resultados.amarillo: There are signs your well-being is starting to depend a lot on another person. Recognizing it early helps you regain your own center.
resultados.rojo: Your well-being and decisions depend too much on another person, and that hurts. In therapy you work on self-esteem and boundaries so you can connect without losing yourself.

familia.descripcion: The DSM-5 includes problems in relationships with relatives: discord, misunderstandings or poor communication among parents, children and siblings. Not a disorder in itself, but it can cause real distress and deserves attention.
preguntas: At home there are frequent arguments or a tense atmosphere.
I feel my family doesn't listen to me or understand me.
I avoid family gatherings or conversations to avoid fights.
There are important subjects nobody dares to talk about.
I feel I carry more responsibilities than the others.
Family conflicts affect my mood, my work or my relationship.

resultados.verde: Family life seems manageable for now. Continuing to talk with clarity and respect helps prevent conflict.
resultados.amarillo: There is tension at home that you already feel. A guided conversation can help everyone listen to each other better.
resultados.rojo: Family conflicts are already affecting your mood and daily life. A professional space helps you set limits, communicate better and look after yourself within the family.

duelo.descripcion: After the death of a loved one, the DSM-5-TR describes prolonged grief disorder: intense longing and emotional pain lasting over a year (six months in children) that limit your life. Other losses can hurt too.
preguntas: I think about what I lost almost every day and find it hard to accept.
I feel a sadness or longing that does not ease with time.
I find it hard to talk about that loss or, on the contrary, I can't talk about anything else.
I have withdrawn from people or activities that used to do me good.
I feel guilt, anger or things left unsaid.
I have felt that I don't want to go on without what I lost.

resultados.verde: You are going through your loss with a certain balance. Give the pain time and room: there is no right way to grieve.
resultados.amarillo: The pain of your loss is still very present and is starting to limit parts of your life. Sharing it with someone who listens can ease the load.
resultados.rojo: The loss is weighing heavily on you and it may be hard to hold yourself up. You don't have to go through this grief alone: being accompanied can give a place to what you feel.

sentido.descripcion: Not a DSM-5 disorder. It is an existential concern: feeling empty or without direction or purpose. It sometimes accompanies depression or a life transition, and talking it through with a professional helps give it direction.
preguntas: I feel my days are all alike and lead nowhere.
I'm not clear about what I want or what matters to me.
What I do feels empty, even though everything looks fine from the outside.
I feel I live to meet other people's expectations.
I find it hard to imagine my future with hope.
I have felt that my life has no value or that I am a burden.

resultados.verde: For now you feel some direction in your life. Setting aside time for what matters to you helps keep it.
resultados.amarillo: There are signs of emptiness or lack of direction worth exploring. Asking yourself what you want is a good starting point, and it is easier with company.
resultados.rojo: You feel an emptiness or lack of purpose that already weighs heavily. Talking it through with a professional can help you regain direction and look after yourself along the way.

migracion.descripcion: The DSM-5 recognizes acculturation problems (adapting to another culture), and distress after migrating can be an adjustment disorder: homesickness, loneliness and a sense of mismatch with your new life that affect daily life.
preguntas: I miss my country, my family or my customs a lot, and being far away hurts.
I feel lonely, even when there are people around me.
I find it hard to adapt to the language, the culture or the way of working here.
I feel I lost my place, my status or who I was before migrating.
I doubt my decision to leave or feel guilty for leaving others behind.
Being far away has drained my mood, my sleep or my desire to do things.

resultados.verde: Your adjustment to another country seems to be going with some balance. Keeping ties with your people and building new ones helps sustain it.
resultados.amarillo: Missing home and feeling out of place already show in your day-to-day. It is understandable, and talking about it keeps migration grief from settling in.
resultados.rojo: Being far from your country is costing you a lot of mood and energy. Being accompanied by someone who understands migration helps give a place to what you left and what you are building.

verde: Repeat this check-in if you notice changes over the coming weeks.
Keep looking after your rest, your movement and your contact with people you trust.
If you want to prevent problems or know yourself better, you can book a free listening session.
amarillo: Talk about what you feel with someone you trust this week.
Pick one small thing you can change right now: sleeping better, setting a limit or taking a break.
Consider booking a first session to work on it with support.
rojo: Book a session soon: there is no need to wait until you feel worse.
Tell someone close to you how you feel so you are not alone.

aviso-de-privacidad.intro: This notice explains what personal data Senderomente handles, what we use it for and what your rights are. It is based on Colombia's Law 1581 of 2012 and Decree 1377 of 2013, and on any other data protection rules that apply.

secciones.titulo: 1. Who is responsible for your data
texto: Ps. Pablo Gómez (Senderomente), located in Australia.
Email: contacto@senderomente.com. You can also write to us on the WhatsApp number shown on the Contact page.
Depending on how you use the service, we may handle:
lista: Identification and contact data: name, email, WhatsApp, country, language and age.
Details of the parent or legal guardian when the person receiving care is under 18.
Whatever you choose to tell us about your reason for seeking help (optional).
Data about your appointments and payments. Stripe processes payments: we never see or store your card details.
Data about your psychological process (clinical record), kept outside this website.
Basic technical data logged by the website host, and two cookies: one remembers your language and the other avoids showing you the quiz again for 24 hours.

texto: Your answers to the orientation quiz and the traffic-light check-ins are not saved or sent. In this version, the website forms do not store what you type; your data is handled when you book, pay, write to us or sign the consent form.

Information about your health, including mental health, is sensitive data. You are not obliged to provide it. We handle it only with your express authorization and to provide psychological care, under professional confidentiality.

secciones.titulo: 5. What we use your data for
lista: Booking, confirming, rescheduling and holding your sessions.
Managing payments and membership.
Providing psychological care and keeping the clinical record.
Answering your questions and registering you for workshops when you ask.
Meeting legal obligations and acting when there is a risk to your life or someone else's.
cierre: We don't sell your data or use it for third-party advertising.

texto: Data about minors is handled with the authorization of a parent or legal guardian, listening to the minor's view according to age and maturity, and respecting their best interests and rights.

secciones.titulo: 7. Providers and transfers to other countries
texto: To operate we use third-party services that may store data outside Colombia and your country:
lista: Vercel (website hosting).
Cal.com (appointment booking).
Stripe (payments).
Google (email, calendar, video calls and consent form).
WhatsApp, by Meta (messages, if you choose to write to us).
cierre: Each provider also applies its own privacy policy. By accepting this notice you authorize these transfers as far as needed to provide the service.

texto: Contact and appointment data are kept as long as needed for the service or required by law. The clinical record is kept for at least 15 years after the last session, under Colombian rules (Resolution 839 of 2017).
You can:
lista: See, update and correct your data.
Ask for proof of the authorization you gave and how your data has been used.
Withdraw your authorization or ask for deletion, when there is no legal duty to keep the data.
Access your data free of charge.
Complain to Colombia's Superintendence of Industry and Commerce, or to the authority in your country.

texto: Write to contacto@senderomente.com with your name, your request and a way to reply. Queries are answered within 10 business days, extendable by 5. Claims are answered within 15 business days, extendable by 8. If we need longer, we will tell you.

We apply reasonable measures to protect your data, although no system is completely foolproof. If we change this notice, we will publish the new version on this page with its date; if the change affects the purposes, we will ask for a new authorization.

consentimiento-informado.intro: Before starting a psychological process we want you to know how it works, what to expect and what its limits are. You accept it on the website when booking and sign it on our form before your first session.

texto: Ps. Pablo Gómez, a psychologist registered in Colombia (COLPSIC). He is not registered in Australia (AHPRA). Care is online and open to people in different countries. Rules on remote psychological care differ from one country to another: if requirements where you are do not allow us to see you, we will tell you and point you to another option.
Online psychological support by video call, in 50-minute sessions. We also offer a free 10-minute listening session to guide you, which is not a therapy session.
The process is voluntary and needs your active participation. No specific results are guaranteed, because they depend on many personal and contextual factors.
Therapy can help you understand what you are going through, build tools and make decisions. Along the way uncomfortable emotions or difficult memories may come up; you can talk about it at any time.
By accepting remote care you understand that there may be connection or device failures and that privacy also depends on where you are. We ask you to:
lista: Connect from a private place with a good connection, and never while driving.
Tell us which city and country you are in at the start of each session.
Give us a trusted emergency contact.
If the call drops, rejoin with the same link or message us on WhatsApp.
cierre: If we consider online care unsuitable for your case, we will point you to in-person care or another service.

secciones.titulo: 5. This is not an emergency service
texto: If you are in danger or thinking about hurting yourself, don't wait for your appointment: use the “Crisis help” button or call your country's emergency line.
What you share in sessions is confidential and protected by professional secrecy (Colombian Law 1090 of 2006). It may only be limited in these cases, sharing only what is strictly necessary:
lista: Risk to you or to others.
Legal obligations or an order from a competent authority.
Situations related to the protection of children and teenagers.

texto: Sessions are not recorded. Please don't record or share them without written permission. Clinical notes are kept outside this website, in a protected system, for the period required by law (at least 15 years after the last session).
We see minors of any age, always with the authorization of a parent or legal guardian. The process is explained to the minor in age-appropriate words and their agreement is taken into account.

The family receives general information about the process and is told if there is any risk. Details the minor shares are handled confidentially, according to their age and well-being. With teenagers, family participation is part of the process.

lista: To offer an ethical, respectful, confidential, safe and non-judgmental space.
To act according to professional principles.
To explain clearly the scope and limits of the process.
To refer you to another professional or service when needed.

texto: You can ask anything you need, decline to answer, request a referral and end the process whenever you decide. Withdrawing your consent does not affect what was done before.
Sessions are paid in advance through the platform. The rules for rescheduling and cancelling are in the Cancellation policy, which is part of this consent.

By accepting and signing you declare that you have read and understood this information, that you could ask questions and that you freely consent to receive online psychological care. If it concerns a minor, you declare this as their parent or legal guardian.
Authorization to handle your personal data is explained and accepted separately in the Privacy notice.

politica-de-cancelacion.intro: We know unexpected things happen. These rules protect your time, other people's and the professional's.

lista: You can reschedule with at least 24 hours' notice, at no cost.
Use the link in your confirmation email, or write to contacto@senderomente.com or on WhatsApp.
Your payment carries over to the new date. No refunds are given for cancellations by the client.

texto: If you give less than 24 hours' notice or don't attend, the session is charged in full and counts as held.
If you are late, the session ends at the scheduled time. If you are more than 15 minutes late, it may be treated as cancelled and charged in full.
If we have to cancel, we will offer you a new date at no cost. If none works for you, we refund that session. If a session is interrupted by a failure on our side, we will make up the time.

secciones.titulo: 5. Membership of 4 or 8 sessions a month
lista: It renews every month until you cancel.
Unused sessions roll over to the following month. If still unused that month, they expire.
You can cancel at any time before the renewal date; the next charge will not be made.
A month already paid is not refunded. If you cancel, you can use pending sessions until the end of the following month.
The free listening session for new people costs nothing. If you can't attend, cancel it so someone else can use the slot.
Members' 2 weekly slots are counted when booked and don't carry over to another week. If you cancel with 24 hours' notice, you get the slot back.
